root_cause.text: Lack of validation of the device-supplied `num_touch_reports` field, allowing a malicious device to specify a value larger than the `touch_reports` array size, causing out-of-bounds read in `dualshock4_parse_report`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch clamps `num_touch_reports` using `min_t(u8, ...)` to `ARRAY_SIZE(usb->touch_reports)` (and similarly for BT path). The commit message states: "the loop in dualshock4_parse_report will read off the end of the touch_reports array" and "Protect against this by clamping the num_touch_reports value provided by the device to the maximum size of the touch_reports array."

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against out-of-bounds access by clamping num_touch_reports to the array size of touch_reports.
intent_record.what: Changed assignment of num_touch_reports from directly using usb->num_touch_reports to using min_t() to clamp it to the maximum allowed by the size of the touch_reports array.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the variable num_touch_reports is now limited to the smaller of the stored value and the number of elements in usb->touch_reports, preventing potential array index out-of-bounds access when touch_reports is later used with num_touch_reports.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the number of touch reports to the array size to prevent potential out-of-bounds access when reading touch reports from Bluetooth DualShock4 packets.
intent_record.what: Changed assignment of num_touch_reports from bt->num_touch_reports to min_t(u8, bt->num_touch_reports, ARRAY_SIZE(bt->touch_reports)).
intent_record.how: This clamps the value of num_touch_reports to not exceed the size of the touch_reports array, ensuring safe array indexing.
